title: Almost disjoint families: many subsets with small intersections

based_on.title: Forcing Summer School Lecture Notes
based_on.pages: 5–6 (§2, Definition 2.3, Proposition 2.4 and Lemma 2.5; infinite-family hypotheses clarified)

summary: Allowing finite overlaps produces continuum many infinite subsets of the naturals.
abstract: A family of pairwise disjoint nonempty subsets of the natural numbers is countable. Allowing finite intersections changes this: a family of infinite subsets can have as many members as there are real numbers. Every countably infinite such family can be enlarged while preserving finite intersections between distinct members. Assuming the axiom of choice, it can be extended to a family that admits no further infinite subset, and such a maximal family can have the full size of the real numbers.
